title: Add sparse four-endpoint observability census
body:
## Summary

This exact observability census extends the two pinned orientations of the PR2979 word from pairs and triples to all `49 choose 4 = 211,876` four-class supports of rank-seven endpoints. A complete GF(3) screen finds 1,353 candidates, each rechecked over the rationals. Six new scalar readout identities span the same five-dimensional block; four use five input coordinates, and all use nine terminal registers across seven endpoint classes.

## Scope and limits

The census shows that these pooled observations expose eligible forms, but the rank-nine join is not a free common helper. These are linear-information identities, not a supplier or caller-facing construction. No downstream consumer, physical realization, complete recursive invoice, or κ improvement is claimed; the selected κ remains `0.001672660197076918`.

The next step is to trace the six-form block to a named downstream caller and compare the caller's required subspace with the five-dimensional span. Only if a caller matches should the multi-register circuit, chronology, dirty-state restoration, storage and recursive profile be priced.

## Test plan

Replayed with Python 3.12:

```sh
python3 -B research/cross-endframe-observability/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/cross-endframe-observability --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/cross-endframe-observability
```

The verifier reconstructs both pinned word orientations and exact formal-warp adjoints; checks endpoint singletons, 1,176 pairs, 18,424 triples and all 211,876 quartets; screens over GF(3) and rechecks every candidate over `Q`. The orientations agree, and protected-column, warp-word and register-deletion controls challenge the witnesses. No physical or recursive invoice is established.

## Sources and credit

Task `complex-new-helper-inventory`, priority revision 6; scope changed to test whether pooling incomparable endpoint observations yields a sparse basis. Package: `research/cross-endframe-observability/`; base commit `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`; both word inputs are hash-pinned in `SOURCES.json`.

[PR #3172](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3172) states the fixed-endpoint pooling boundary tested here. The package extends the changed PR2979 word and makes no general novelty claim. The cached overlap scan covered 394 open PRs and 2,319 discussions as of 2026-10-18 03:15 UTC, but refresh failed and this is not a novelty certificate. Provider attribution from PR #2979 and the stated pooling boundary from PR #3172 are retained. Prepared by OpenAI Codex with substantial AI assistance; no independent human or formal-kernel review is claimed. Apache-2.0.
